card: This pull request introduces the setprunelock and listprunelocks RPC methods and a -prunelockheight startup argument to allow manual control over block pruning locks. It solves the issue on pruned nodes where unloading a wallet or taking an external application offline can result in needed historical blocks being pruned, preventing future rescans. The change exposes the existing internal prune lock mechanism with a dedicated user prefix without persisting locks across restarts. There are no prerequisite or dependent pull requests.
changed_since_previous: Now includes the complete implementation diff containing the RPC implementations in src/rpc/blockchain.cpp, startup logic in src/init.cpp, and functional tests in test/functional/rpc_prunelock.py.
evidence: PR description: "On pruned nodes, if a wallet is not loaded while the node is running, blocks necessary for rescanning when the wallet is loaded may be pruned. This PR allows users and external wallet software to manually manage prune locks via RPC, so they can protect blocks needed for future rescans and also clean up locks that are no longer relevant"
problem: On pruned nodes, blocks needed for a wallet rescan can be pruned away if the wallet is unloaded while the node runs and syncs new blocks. External wallets and services using Bitcoin Core as a backend also lack an interface to protect a range of block files from automatic pruning during temporary downtime.

risk.why: A bug in prune lock enforcement could either prune data that was requested to be preserved or inhibit pruning entirely and exhaust disk space.

scope_notes: Adds two new RPC commands and one command-line argument, backed by the existing BlockManager prune lock mechanism.
summary: This pull request adds the setprunelock and listprunelocks RPCs, along with a -prunelockheight startup option, allowing users and external software to manage block prune locks. These locks instruct the block storage manager not to prune blocks at or above a specified height, using a memory-only "user:" prefix to prevent collisions with internal index locks.
